description.value: Ruckle Park occupies Salt Spring Island's southeastern shore with seven kilometres of rocky headlands, tidal pools, and grassy meadows overlooking Swanson Channel; ferry access is required and potable water is shut off November 1–March 15.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies 8 RV/caravan sites within Ruckle Provincial Park on Salt Spring Island, with explicit tags noting no power supply, no internet access, and no sanitary dump station; however, per the rules these OSM amenity tags are not treated as authoritative without website confirmation. The BC Parks website confirms the park is active and operational, notes a seasonal potable water system (shut down Nov 1–Mar 15, implying it is available the rest of the year), and confirms reservations are accepted via camping.bcparks.ca or by phone. No cyclist-specific amenities, showers, food services, or charging infrastructure are mentioned anywhere on the website.
concerns: OSM community field lists 'Sidney' but Ruckle Park is located on Salt Spring Island, not in Sidney — likely a geographic community-assignment error in the OSM data.
No address or phone number present in the OSM record; only general BC Parks system-wide contact information is available on the website.

This record covers only the RV/caravan section (sites 1–8); separate OSM records may exist for tent or walk-in camping areas within the same park, which could result in fragmented or duplicate directory listings.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Ruckle Park is a legitimate, well-known provincial park on Salt Spring Island that touring cyclists navigating the Gulf Islands ferry network would directly benefit from knowing about; the RV sites are a clearly delineated section of an active campground.
enrichment_extras.notes: The park also contains tent and walk-in camping areas not represented by this OSM record. An active farm portion of the park is closed to the public. Dogs are restricted from certain trail sections due to ongoing livestock interactions.
